title: BETWEEN THE GIANTS
alt: A nun walking between the monumental columns of the Vatican
story_en: Everything around her was built to endure. Yet the smallest thing in the photograph was the one that was alive.
story_fr: Tout, autour d’elle, a été bâti pour durer. Pourtant, la plus petite chose de la photographie était celle qui vivait.

title: A THOUSAND LITTLE SUNS
alt: Tokyo at night, a wall of illuminated signs
story_en: Every light wanted to be seen. Somewhere in the noise, I discovered the beauty of being anonymous.
story_fr: Chaque lumière voulait être vue. Quelque part dans ce bruit, j’ai découvert la beauté d’être anonyme.

title: THE STREET THAT REMEMBERS
alt: A funicular climbing a steep street in Lisbon
story_en: Some cities move forward. Others allow the past to travel alongside us.
story_fr: Certaines villes avancent. D’autres laissent le passé voyager à nos côtés.

title: A MOMENT OF REFLECTION
alt: Two goats standing apart on a canal bank, mirrored in the water, against a lichen-covered brick wall
story_en: Two goats, each on its own little pedestal, looking away from each other. Only the water brought them together.
story_fr: Deux chèvres, chacune sur son petit piédestal, qui ne se regardent pas. Seule l'eau les a réunies.

title: SOMEWHERE BETWEEN DARWIN AND BROOME
alt: A full moon rising over silhouetted bush and tall grasses in a pink dusk sky
story_en: Hours of empty road. Then the moon came up, and nowhere became a place to stop.
story_fr: Des heures de route vide. Puis la lune s'est levée, et ce nulle part est devenu un endroit où s'arrêter.

title: IN BARCELONA, WE LEARNED TO TRUST
alt: A forest of TV antennas on Barcelona rooftops at sunset
story_en: Every roof was listening for something. Up there, among the antennas, I learned to trust what I could not see.
story_fr: Chaque toit écoutait quelque chose. Là-haut, parmi les antennes, j'ai appris à faire confiance à ce que je ne voyais pas.

title: DO ME A FAVOR
alt: Rows of colourful lucha libre wrestling masks hanging on a market stall
story_en: A wall of faces, and not one of them real. Here, a mask does not hide who you are. It is who you become.
story_fr: Un mur de visages, et pas un seul de vrai. Ici, le masque ne cache pas qui l'on est. Il est ce que l'on devient.

title: FROM UP HERE, EVERYTHING IS QUIET
alt: Alfama rooftops and the white dome of the National Pantheon, Lisbon, framed by columns and bougainvillea
story_en: From up here, the city looks finished. Down there, it is still being lived.
story_fr: D'ici, la ville semble achevée. En bas, on est encore en train de la vivre.

title: WHAT WE OFFER TO THE DAY
alt: Balinese palm-leaf offerings with burning incense on a stone wall above rice terraces
story_en: Every morning, someone makes a small gift for the day, knowing it will not last. The smoke rises anyway.
story_fr: Chaque matin, quelqu'un fait un petit cadeau à la journée, en sachant qu'il ne durera pas. La fumée monte quand même.

title: THE SKY HELD ITS BREATH
alt: A red paper lantern against a clear blue sky, Osaka
story_en: One red lantern, and all that sky around it. The frame needed nothing else.
story_fr: Une lanterne rouge, et tout ce ciel autour. Le cadre n’avait besoin de rien d’autre.

title: AN UNFINISHED CONVERSATION
alt: Two maiko in kimono looking into the camera, Kyoto
story_en:
They stopped and looked straight at me.
For one second, the conversation was between the three of us.
It never really ended.
story_fr:
Elles se sont arrêtées et m’ont regardée.
Pendant une seconde, la conversation s’est faite à trois.
Elle ne s’est jamais vraiment terminée.

title: OUR FLAGS WERE DRYING
alt: A Lisbon façade with laundry hanging from the windows
story_en: Nobody hung these clothes to make something beautiful. Beauty was never waiting for permission.
story_fr: Personne n’a étendu ce linge pour faire quelque chose de beau. La beauté n’a jamais attendu de permission.

title: THE VALUE OF WHAT REMAINS
alt: Flakes of gold leaf scattered on cracked stone
story_en: I was interested not in what had been offered, but in what remained.
story_fr: Ce qui m’intéressait, ce n’était pas ce qui avait été offert, mais ce qui restait.

title: THE LAST LIGHT BELONGS TO NO ONE
alt: An orange sunset over the horizon
story_en: For a few seconds, the entire world seemed to be holding its breath.
story_fr: Pendant quelques secondes, le monde entier a semblé retenir son souffle.

title: BLUE, INTERRUPTED
alt: A single white contrail crossing a clear blue sky
story_en:
For a moment, the entire sky seemed to have been drawn with a single line.
Nothing stayed. Except the photograph.
story_fr:
Un instant, le ciel entier a semblé dessiné d’un seul trait.
Rien n’est resté. Sauf la photographie.

title: THE CAT KNEW
alt: A black cat sitting on cobblestones
story_en: It did not move, and it did not look away. Of the two of us, it was the one who belonged there.
story_fr: Il n’a pas bougé, il n’a pas détourné les yeux. De nous deux, c’était lui qui était chez lui.

title: EVERYBODY IS GOING SOMEWHERE
alt: The legs of passers-by walking in a street
story_en: I only kept their steps. Each of them was on the way to a life I will never know.
story_fr: Je n’ai gardé que leurs pas. Chacun allait vers une vie que je ne connaîtrai jamais.

title: AN OFFERING TO THE DAY
alt: A Thai shrine crowded with small Buddha figures and offerings
story_en: Some gestures are repeated every morning, for no one in particular. This one stayed.
story_fr: Certains gestes se répètent chaque matin, pour personne en particulier. Celui-ci est resté.

title: THE TREE KEPT THE SUN
alt: A twisted tree in silhouette against a burning sunset
story_en: The sun went down behind it. For a moment, the tree seemed to be holding what was left.
story_fr: Le soleil s’est couché derrière lui. Un instant, l’arbre a semblé retenir ce qui restait.

title: SAIGONESE MOTORBIKE FEVER
alt: Saigon traffic at night, a river of motorbikes in motion
story_en:
Thousands of engines, all going somewhere at once.
I stood still on the corner and let the city pour past me.
story_fr:
Des milliers de moteurs, tous pressés d’aller quelque part.
Je suis resté immobile au coin de la rue, et j’ai laissé la ville couler devant moi.

title: TWICE UPON A TIME
alt: Twin girls in white áo dài riding bicycles side by side, Saigon
story_en:
I photographed them together.
Only years later did I realise they were twins.
Sometimes a photograph knows something before the person who made it does.
story_fr:
Je les ai photographiées ensemble.
Ce n’est que des années plus tard que j’ai compris qu’elles étaient jumelles.
Parfois, une photographie sait quelque chose avant celle qui l’a prise.

title: THE WOMEN WHO WERE THERE
alt: Two women at the entrance of a small grocery shop, Saigon
story_en: I do not know their stories. But for one fraction of a second, our lives met. And all these years later, they are still here.
story_fr: Je ne connais pas leurs histoires. Mais pendant une fraction de seconde, nos vies se sont croisées. Et toutes ces années plus tard, elles sont toujours là.

title: THE CITY RESTS WHERE IT CAN
alt: A man asleep across a row of parked scooters, Saigon
story_en: In a city that never seemed to stop, he found somewhere to be still.
story_fr: Dans une ville qui ne semblait jamais s’arrêter, il avait trouvé où rester immobile.

title: THE NIGHT WRITES BACK
alt: City lights at night, drawn into moving lines by a long exposure
story_en: The camera could not hold the city still. What looked like a mistake became another way of seeing.
story_fr: L’appareil n’a pas su retenir la ville. Ce qui ressemblait à une erreur est devenu une autre manière de voir.

title: WALKING TOGETHER
alt: A group in black robes and conical straw hats crossing a street, Japan
story_en: For a moment, another time seemed to pass through the present.
story_fr: Un instant, un autre temps a semblé traverser le présent.

title: STRANGERS IN PASSING
alt: A black-and-white street scene with passers-by
story_en: None of them saw me. For one second, they all belonged to the same picture.
story_fr: Aucun d’eux ne m’a vue. Pendant une seconde, ils ont tous appartenu à la même image.

title: THE MOMENT BETWEEN MOMENTS
alt: A white statue on a tall pedestal in a garden, a man standing small below it, black and white
story_en: Nothing decisive happens here. Perhaps that is the moment.
story_fr: Rien de décisif ne se passe ici. C’est peut-être cela, l’instant.

title: THE WORLD CAN WAIT
alt: A man asleep stretched out on his motorbike against a grey metal wall, traffic passing behind, black and white
story_en:
His motorbike was his bed, the handlebars his pillow.
Behind him, the city kept rushing past.
He had decided it could wait.
story_fr:
Sa moto était son lit, le guidon son oreiller.
Derrière lui, la ville continuait de filer.
Il avait décidé qu’elle pouvait attendre.

title: EVERYTHING HERE IS PARKED
alt: A man asleep across a long row of parked scooters, seen from above, black and white
story_en:
Dozens of machines, waiting in a row.
One of them had brought a man along.
He was waiting too.
story_fr:
Des dizaines de machines, alignées, qui attendent.
L’une d’elles avait amené un homme.
Lui aussi attendait.

title: THE WALL HOLDS US UP
alt: Workers resting barefoot along a brick wall, one in a hard hat, black and white
story_en:
Midday. Nobody had planned to stop together.
The wall did it for them.
One of them looked up and laughed.
story_fr:
Midi. Personne n’avait prévu de s’arrêter ensemble.
Le mur l’a fait pour eux.
L’un d’eux a levé les yeux et a ri.

title: ALL THE VOICES OF THE STREET
alt: A utility pole at night buried in cables, car lights streaking past below
story_en:
Every call, every light, every voice of the street passed through this one pole.
I could not hear any of it.
I could see all of it.
story_fr:
Chaque appel, chaque lumière, chaque voix de la rue passait par ce seul poteau.
Je n’en entendais rien.
Je voyais tout.

title: SEEN THROUGH THE KNOT
alt: A night street seen through a dense curtain of cables, passers-by blurred in the light
story_en:
I looked down at the street through the cables, the way you look through branches.
Life was down there, tangled and bright.
story_fr:
J’ai regardé la rue à travers les câbles, comme on regarde à travers des branches.
La vie était en bas, emmêlée et lumineuse.

title: SOMEONE KNOWS WHICH ONE
alt: A worker on a bamboo ladder reaching into a huge tangle of black cables, pink flowers below
story_en:
Thousands of wires, and one man on a ladder.
Somehow, he knew which one.
story_fr:
Des milliers de fils, et un homme sur une échelle.
Il savait, on ne sait comment, lequel était le bon.

title: BETWEEN THE WALLS
alt: Teal apartment building and narrow alley in Saigon seen from an upper balcony
story_en: High above the alley, the city holds its breath in layers of plaster, balconies and quiet light.
story_fr: Au-dessus de la ruelle, la ville retient son souffle entre façades, balcons et lumière calme.

title: TWO GREEN CUBS
alt: Two vintage green Honda Cub motorbikes parked side by side against a weathered wall, Saigon
story_en: Two green machines resting against a flaking wall. Always ready to carry the city a little further.
story_fr: Deux machines vertes posées contre un mur usé. Toujours prêtes à porter la ville un peu plus loin.
